title: H100/L40S auto-profile generator and clock-orchestration for prefill/decode kernel routing
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Problem: Certain long-sequence prefill workloads and mixed short/long decode mixes show suboptimal kernel selection and excessive latency variance on H100 and L40S hosts when running across heterogeneous MIG partitions and clock domains. We need a lightweight, deterministic mechanism that generates per-host auto-profiles (clock + kernel preference) derived from a small workload fingerprint and uses that to steer prefill vs decode kernel routing with minimal runtime overhead.

Goal: Ship an internal service that: (1) collects a short micro-workload fingerprint at deployment time, (2) produces an auto-profile recommending clock targets and kernel candidates for prefill and decode phases, (3) exposes a runtime policy for the scheduler to select kernels and clock targets by request class, and (4) provides safe fallbacks and telemetry to measure regressions in latency and throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Auto-profile generator produces stable profile for the same host within 5% variance across repeated runs
End-to-end tail latency (p99) for benchmark prefill/length-2048 workload improves by >=10% on H100 when using profile-driven clock targets and kernel routing compared to baseline
No >5% throughput regression for mixed short (<=64) + long (>=1024) decode workloads on L40S with MIG partitioning enabled
Profiles are stored and versioned; rollout supports canary for 10% of requests and immediate rollback
Telemetry surfaces per-host profile id, selected kernel, selected clock target, and delta vs baseline in Console dashboards
design_decisions: Profile generator will run as a short-lived init task during node boot or container start; avoids continuous sampling to reduce jitter
Fingerprint = distribution of sequence lengths + tokenization overhead + small synthetic prefill/decode runs (<=5 samples)
Profiles map to: preferred kernel family (e.g., fast-attn-vec, chunked-kv-cache), preferred quantization path, and clock target bucket (nominal, perf, eco)
Scheduler will consult a per-host profile cache and request-class tags (prefill-heavy, decode-heavy, low-latency) to select kernel + clock target
Clock changes are orchestrated through staged APIs with governor enforcement and bounded ramp windows to avoid thermal oscillation
Fallback chain: profile -> last-successful kernel -> generic safe kernel. Clock target fallback to nominal if thermal/PMU errors observed
test_plan: Unit tests for profile generator parsing and mapping rules
Hardware integration tests on H100/L40S/A10 lab racks: run benchmark matrix (seq=32/256/1024/2048) with MIG partitions 1/2/7
A/B canary on dedicated cluster: 10% traffic for 48 hours comparing profile-driven routing vs baseline
Stability test: 72-hour steady-run with mixed workload to confirm no thermal-triggered throttling regressions
SLO check: automated alert if p99 latency regresses >7% during canary
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal QA on canary racks (today -> +2w)
Phase 2: Canary on non-production customers (10% traffic, 48h)
Phase 3: Ramp to 50% with monitoring guardrails (automatic rollback on regression)
Phase 4: Full rollout and enable profile storage retention for 90 days
risks: Frequent clock toggles could increase thermal cycling and reduce hardware lifespan if not rate-limited
Profile mismatch for workloads that vary rapidly at runtime leading to misrouting and latency spikes
Edge cases on A10 where certain kernels are memory-bound and profile recommendations may harm throughput
Complexity in integrating profile selection into existing scheduler without adding per-request expensive checks
dependencies: observability: add profile-id and selected-kernel traces to request-span
